headline: Formal models for compositionality, batch effects, and uncertainty in omics inference
label: Statistical Models For Omics Data
summary: Omics datasets with compositional structure, batch effects, and high dimensionality demand explicit uncertainty quantification.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit statistical modeling of structure that complicates inference in high-throughput omics data. Several items address compositionality directly: a bias analysis of proportionality metrics on count compositional data, iterative reference selection for microbiome normalization, and a logit-normal multinomial model. Others pair robust Bayesian or nonparametric formulations with inference, including GLORB for RNA-seq differential expression under global expression shifts, SEcov for microbiome co-occurrence networks, and SigClust-LCP for significance testing of scRNA-seq clustering. Covariate integration appears in supervised microbiome dimension reduction, NExON-Bayes network estimation with ordinal covariates, and batch-effect removal in COBRA and NDreamer. Several benchmarking studies provide comparative assessment, and evidence scope varies across the set. The new element is formal uncertainty quantification combined with covariate integration.
